text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — code freeze for 1.14.0 starts in ~3 hours at 22:00 UTC. If you need a late merge, post the PR link + one-line risk summary + rollback plan + approver(s). We'll triage immediately. Exceptions only for critical bug fixes or legal/marketing doc fixes that can't wait. :warning:

Sam: Small runtime flag bump required for perf tests — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 — low risk, unit tests green, no schema changes. Rollback: revert commit + redeploy prior image. Requesting approvals: @Devon @Ira

Maya: Thanks Sam — pinged approvers. Please add the label `freeze-exception` and include the template below so triage is faster.

Maya: ```
PR: <link>
Risk (low/med/high):
Why after cutoff: (why this couldn't land before freeze)
Rollback steps: (commands + image/tag to restore)
Approvers: @name @name
```

Devon: I reviewed runtime PR 5123 — low risk, looks safe. I approve. Please ensure a quick staging smoke after merge. :+1:

Ira: QA can do a focused smoke on staging in ~20m, will report back within 30m. If smoke passes and CI is green, LGTM from QA.

Carla: For changelog — add a one-liner under "bug fixes" and mention perf impact. I can fold it into the release notes after the merge. :memo:

Sam: will add label and changelog entry now.

Maya: Great. Two other asks in the queue look higher risk; I'll triage those next. If we don't get approvers for them we'll hold and schedule a hotpatch window tomorrow morning.

release-bot: Code freeze scheduled at 1972509600 (22:00 UTC). Any merges after that without an approved `freeze-exception` will be reverted automatically. :lock:

Maya: TL;DR — if you need a late merge: use the template, add `freeze-exception`, ping approvers, include rollback steps. We'll keep the window tight. :eyes:
